import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders for safe formatting. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_name} Invitation
{event_name}
Date: {date_of_event}
{description_of_event}
{notes_block} """ def create_invitation_for_event( event_name: str, description_of_event: str, date_of_event: str, notes_for_event: str ) -> str: """ Generates a sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- event_name : str Title of the event. description_of_event : str Detailed description (may contain newlines). date_of_event : str Scheduled date of the event. notes_for_event : str Extra instructions or information. Returns ------- str A complete HTML document with all user-supplied content escaped. Raises ------ ValueError If any required argument is missing or empty. """ # Basic validation if not all([event_name, description_of_event, date_of_event]): raise ValueError("Event name, description, and date must be provided.") # Escape all user-controlled input to prevent XSS safe_event_name = html.escape(event_name, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(description_of_event, quote=True) safe_date = html.escape(date_of_event, quote=True) # Optional notes block: only include if not empty if notes_for_event: safe_notes = html.escape(notes_for_event, quote=True) notes_block = f'
Notes:
{safe_notes}
' else: notes_block = '' # Format the final HTML invitation_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_name=safe_event_name, description_of_event=safe_description, date_of_event=safe_date, notes_block=notes_block ) return invitation_html.strip()
